questions.knowledge_point: Calculating dy/dx at a Point Using dx/dy
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y\sqrt{y}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+2y) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+2y) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2})-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{y}^{1/2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2y+2 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{y}-y+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{y}-y+2}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(8,4),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(8,4)} & =\frac{1}{(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{4}-4+2)}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Tangent Line Using dx/dy
questions.problem: Given a curve $x=y+\frac{3}{{y}^{3}},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y+\frac{3}{{y}^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-3}) \\  & =1+3\cdot (-3{y}^{-4}) \\  & =1-9{y}^{-4} \\  & =1-\frac{9}{{y}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{{y}^{4}-9}{{y}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{4}}{{y}^{4}-9}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(4,1)} \\  & =\frac{{1}^{4}}{{1}^{4}-9} \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-\frac{1}{8}(x-4) \\ y & =-\frac{x}{8}+\frac{1}{2}+1 \\ y & =-\frac{x}{8}+\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given a curve $x=\sqrt{{y}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(2,1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\sqrt{{y}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\sqrt{{y}^{3}})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{y}^{1/2}-2{y}^{-3} \\  & =\frac{3{y}^{1/2}}{2}-\frac{2}{{y}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{3{y}^{7/2}-4}{2{y}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{2{y}^{3}}{3{y}^{7/2}-4}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(2,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(2,1)} \\  & =\frac{2(1)^{3}}{3(1)^{7/2}-4} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-2(x-2) \\ y & =-2x+4+1 \\ y & =-2x+5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating dy/dx at a Point Using dx/dy
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{4}-\frac{3}{y}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{4})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1}) \\  & =4{y}^{3}-3(-{y}^{-2}) \\  & =4{y}^{3}+3{y}^{-2} \\  & =4{y}^{3}+\frac{3}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4{y}^{5}+3}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{4{y}^{5}+3}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(4,-1),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(4,-1)} & =\frac{(-1)^{2}}{4(-1)^{5}+3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Tangent Line Using dx/dy
questions.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(6\sqrt{y}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\sqrt{y})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{1/2})-2(2y) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{2}{y}^{-1/2}-4y \\  & =3{y}^{-1/2}-4y \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{y}}-4y \\  & =\frac{3-4y\sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{y}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{\sqrt{y}}{3-4y\sqrt{y}}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(4,1)} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1}}{3-4(1)\sqrt{1}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3-4} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-(x-4) \\ y & =-x+4+1 \\ y & =-x+5.\end{aligned}
$$
